questions.questionText:
A student wishes to measure accurately the volume of approximately 40cm3 of water. She has
two measuring cylinders, a larger one that can hold 100cm3, and a smaller one that can hold
50cm3. The water forms a meniscus where it touches the glass.
top of
meniscus
bottom of
meniscus
Which cylinder and which water level does the student use to ensure an accurate result?
cylinder water level

A sealed container of volume 2000cm3 contains air at high pressure.
The container is placed on a top-pan balance.
The balance reads 200.00g.
All the air is removed by a vacuum pump and the balance reading changes to 196.00g.
What was the density of the pressurised air?

A gymnast jumps down from a high piece of apparatus.
She gradually bends her knees as she lands.
Which effect does this have?

options.text: She will have a smaller change of momentum as she lands.
She will lose less kinetic energy as she lands.
She will exert a smaller impulse on the ground as she lands.
She will experience a smaller force from the ground as she lands.

questions.questionText:
The equation p = gh can be used for a liquid.
What is the meaning of the term ?

options.text: total pressure due to the liquid and the air above the liquid
density of an object placed in the liquid

questions.questionText:
What are the correct terms for each change of state?
liquid to solid liquid to gas

Extremely small pollen grains in water are viewed through a microscope. The grains are seen to
move continually and randomly.
What is the reason for this random movement?

options.text: The grains are moved by randomly moving water molecules.
The grains are moved by random convection currents in the water.
The grains are moved by random rays of light reflecting off them.
The grains are moved by the random motion of their own atoms.

questions.questionText: Which effect is caused by thermal expansion?

options.text: a metal surface heating up in direct sunlight
ice-cream melting on a hot day
a railway track buckling on a hot day
ice forming on a pond on a cold day

questions.questionText:
An ice cube is placed in a beaker and is heated.
The ice melts to form water, which evaporates at first and then boils.
The steam condenses on a cold window in the room.
Which process involves a transfer of energy from the ice, water or steam to the surroundings?

Two samples of the same material have the same mass but different surface areas.
Each sample is heated to the same temperature and then left to cool to room temperature.
Each sample is allowed to cool to the same final temperature.
X Y
small surface area large surface area
Which row correctly compares the decrease in internal energy and the initial rate of cooling for
each sample?
decrease in internal energy initial rate of cooling

options.text: X loses more internal energy than Y X cools down faster than Y
Y loses more internal energy than X Y cools down faster than X
X and Y lose the same quantity of energy X cools down faster than Y
X and Y lose the same quantity of energy Y cools down faster than X

questions.questionText: In which type of wave is the direction of vibration parallel to the direction of travel?

Waves in a ripple tank are diffracted as they pass through a narrow gap.
What can be done to make the spreading due to diffraction greater?

options.text: Decrease the frequency of the waves and keep the speed constant.
Decrease the speed of the waves and keep the frequency constant.
Increase the frequency of the waves and keep the speed constant.
Increase the frequency of the waves and decrease the speed.

Thermal radiation is part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
What is the name of this region of the spectrum?
Which statement about the direction of a magnetic field at a point is correct?

options.text: It is the direction of the force on an N pole placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on an S pole placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on a positive charge placed at that point.
It is the direction of the force on a negative charge placed at that point.

W X
Which row shows the correct labels for W, X and Y?
label of W a.c. supply d.c. supply

Two electrical appliances are connected to the mains supply.
The cable connected to one appliance includes an earth wire.
The cable connected to the second appliance does not need an earth wire.
What is a reason for this difference?

options.text: One appliance has a metal case, but the other appliance does not.
One appliance is fitted with a fuse, but the other appliance is not.
One appliance is fitted with a switch, but the other appliance is not.
One appliance needs more current than the other appliance.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a simple a.c. generator. The magnet rotates around a fixed coil wound round
a fixed iron core. The electromotive force (e.m.f.) output is a sine wave, a series of crests, zeros
and troughs.
The magnet is shown in three positions, P, Q and R, during its rotation. The magnetic field in the
coil is zero at Q but changing most rapidly.
position P position Q position R
magnet
N S S N
fixed coil
Which statement about the induced e.m.f. in the coil is correct?

options.text: The magnitude of the e.m.f. at position Q is larger than that at position P.
The magnitude of the e.m.f. at position Q is zero.
The magnitude of the e.m.f. at position Q is smaller than at position R, but not zero.
The magnitude of the e.m.f. at position R is larger than at position P.

type of emission half-life

The Earth orbits the Sun once in approximately 365 days.
The average radius of the orbit is 1.5  1011m.
What is the average orbital speed of the Earth?
Which statement about the life cycle of a star is correct?

options.text: All stars eventually run out of hydrogen as fuel.
A red giant forms a planetary nebula with a supernova at its centre.
A white dwarf star eventually forms a black hole.
Most stars expand and form protostars.
